value.rationale: Unary degree-one nodes are the contraction/subdivision points of the rooted tree, a natural structural statistic for size-conditioned random trees. Their entire adjacent stochastic comparison classification under root outdegree is sharp for every n,k: one near-maximal tail strictly rises as forest component count rises, while the previous maximum disappears; the only exception is the deterministic last comparison. This demonstrates a nontrivial distributional limitation of root-branching order not captured by means or by known leaf-statistic monotonicity.
